title: Relational Correlation Map and Compacting Log Broker
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current ingest pipeline attaches a single correlation id per event and writes verbatim structured JSON to Loki/ELK. Downstream teams often need to join events across multiple id families (request_id, trace_id, session_id, tenant_trace) but the mapping between these ids is lossy and duplicated across services. This makes troubleshooting multi-service latency spikes and error cascades expensive and error-prone.

Proposal: Implement a Relational Correlation Map (RCM) service + Compacting Log Broker (CLB). RCM is a small, strongly-consistent store that records canonical relationships between correlation identifiers observed at ingestion time (edge proxies, runtime sidecars, and ingestion gateways). CLB uses RCM to normalize and compact incoming structured logs before writing to long-term stores (Loki/ELK). "Normalized" means attach a canonical correlation key (rcm_id), deduplicate repetitive log bursts, and emit a compacted event that references original event_ids for downstream retrieval.

Goals: reduce noise by 6x for bursty logs, make trace joins across id families O(1), preserve fidelity for forensic retrieval, and improve dashboard signal-to-noise for latency/error SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: RCM API can create and query id relationships with end-to-end latency under 10ms p95 for local region
CLB compaction reduces token/line write volume to Loki by at least 60% on the provided burst workload replay
All compacted events include rcm_id and a provenance array (list of original event ids) that can be resolved within 60s to full event payloads
No loss of unique error events: QA harness must show 0 false negatives for distinct error signatures across 100k test events
Backward compatible: services not yet upgraded must continue to emit logs and CLB falls back to pass-through mode without correlation enrichment
implementation_notes: RCM: implement as a lightweight Postgres-backed service using a single table (rcm_relations) with natural keys: rcm_id (uuid), id_type, id_value, observed_at, canonical_at. Use upserts on ingest to merge new id families. Add a TTL for cold mappings (configurable per-tenant).

CLB: sits in front of the existing ingest pipeline (edge -> CLB -> transformer -> storage). CLB performs: parse -> normalize ids -> query RCM -> dedup by (rcm_id, signature_hash, time_bucket) -> emit compacted envelope. Provide fast path for known high-throughput tenants using in-memory LRU caches and fall back to remote RCM calls when cache misses occur.

Schema: compacted envelope fields: rcm_id, signature_hash, summary_message, count, first_seen, last_seen, provenance_ids (array of event ids), tenant_id, source_service, severity, sample_rate_meta. Store raw payload pointers in S3/Cold-archive with lifecycle rules so provenance resolution can rehydrate full events.

Tracing hooks: instrument RCM and CLB with OpenTelemetry spans. When CLB calls RCM, attach parent trace and emit correlation logs. Add metrics: rcm_query_p95, clb_compaction_rate, compaction_latency_p95, provenance_resolution_success_rate.

Failure modes: if RCM is unavailable, CLB enters degraded mode and tags events with rcm_unavailable=true and continues in pass-through or best-effort caching. Implement circuit-breaker with exponential backoff and local cache TTL to reduce blast radius.

Backfill: write a snapshot job that scans recent raw logs and populates RCM for common id pairs. Backfill must be throttled and idempotent. Provide a dry-run mode to estimate rcm map growth before full backfill.
Data residency & RBAC: RCM must obey tenant isolation; tenant-scoped rows and column-level encryption for PII-like ids. Integrate with KMS for encryption-at-rest.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy RCM in staging with canary traffic from the edge sidecar for a single engineering tenant. 2) Deploy CLB in front of staging ingest with pass-through as default; enable compaction for the canary tenant. 3) Monitor compaction metrics and dashboard SLOs for 48 hours, validate provenance resolution. 4) Gradual roll to 10% of production tenants over 1 week (automated rollout via Console). 5) Enable global rollout after 2-week stability window and run backfill for top 20 tenants. Provide kill-switch route at routing layer to bypass CLB immediately.
qa_steps: Unit tests for RCM upsert/query semantics and TTL eviction
Integration test: simulate 1M events replay with mixed id families; assert compaction ratio and provenance resolution correctness
Chaos tests: kill RCM and validate CLB degraded-mode behavior and no data loss in storage
Security: run static analysis and verify KMS integration in staging; perform 3rd-party pen test on RCM endpoints
Performance: benchmark RCM p95 under 2k qps and CLB compaction throughput at 10GB/s ingest equivalent in a perf cluster
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: mapping store growth for large tenants could exhaust storage. Mitigation: TTLs, sampling, and tiering of cold mappings to BigTable/Blob store; monitor cardinality with alerts.
Risk: compaction hides individually valuable events (over-aggregation). Mitigation: signature-based rules to always preserve unique error classes and configurable minimum sample retention per tenant.
Risk: added lookup latency may impact ingest p99. Mitigation: LRU cache, local in-memory write coalescing, and async enrichment with eventual resolution flag on initial write.
